content: If you are a resident of the United States, you can contact the Poison Control Center at 1-800-222-1222. If you are in Canada, you can call 1-844-764-7669. While taking this medication, it is essential to undergo regular comprehensive physical examinations. These should include laboratory and/or medical tests such as blood pressure measurements, breast exams, pelvic exams, and Pap smears. Follow your doctor’s instructions on how to perform self-breast examinations, and report any lumps immediately. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, refer to the product package information for specific guidance. You may need to use an additional form of birth control, such as condoms or spermicides, to prevent pregnancy. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in May 2024. Important Note on Usage of This Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Uses: This medication is used to prevent pregnancy. It is commonly referred to as the mini-pill because it does not contain estrogen. While the mini-pill is more effective than certain other methods of birth control (e.g., condoms, cervical caps, diaphragms), it is less effective than combination hormone birth control (which contains both estrogen and progestin) because it does not consistently prevent ovulation. This medication is typically used by women who cannot take estrogen. How to Use: Before starting this medication, read the Patient Information Leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Review it again each time you get a refill. The leaflet contains critical instructions on when to take your pills and what to do if you miss a dose. Take this medication orally as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. If you experience stomach upset or nausea, taking the medication after your evening meal or at bedtime may help. Alternatively, you may choose a time of day that is easier for you to remember. It is best to start taking this medication on the first day of your menstrual period. Continue taking one tablet every day without interruption. After finishing the last tablet in a pack, begin a new pack the next day. There is no break between packs, and you do not take any reminder tablets (tablets without medication). Your menstrual periods may become irregular, heavier, or lighter than usual. You may also experience vaginal bleeding (spotting) between periods. Pregnancy is more likely if you miss pills, start a new pack late, or take your pill at a different time of day than usual. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for advice on switching from other forms of hormonal birth control (e.g., patches, other birth control pills) to this product. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, headache, bloating, breast tenderness, or weight gain. Vaginal bleeding between periods (spotting) or missed/irregular periods may also occur. If any of these effects persist or worsen, inform your doctor or pharmacist promptly. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to you outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Precautions: Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to norethindrone, other progestins, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may cause blotchy, dark areas on your face and skin (melasma). Sunlight can worsen this effect. Limit your time in the sun, and avoid tanning booths and sunlamps. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. It can pass into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some drugs may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control by decreasing the levels of birth control hormones in your body, potentially leading to pregnancy. Examples of such drugs include griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin), ritonavir, and St. John’s Wort. Inform your doctor when starting any new medication, and discuss whether you should use reliable backup birth control. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., sex hormone-binding globulin, thyroid tests), potentially causing false test results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222. In Canada, you can call 1-844-764-7669. Regular Monitoring: While taking this medication, it is important to undergo regular physical exams, including laboratory and medical tests such as blood pressure checks, breast exams, pelvic exams, and Pap smears. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-breast examinations, and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments.
